newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet crude firm despite weaker Brent paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet crude firm despite weaker Brent paper.

text.p: Sustained demand for late January barrels kept North Sea wet crudes steady to a shade firmer on Friday despite softer Brent paper which was pressured by a rise in U.S. stocks, traders said.

Feb Brent shed 25 cents to $23.97 a barrel by 1140 GMT after API data released after the market close Thursday revealed a surprise build in U.S. crude stocks and a bigger than expected rise in distillate inventories.
Falling outright values undermined Brent CFDs and intermonth paper spreads, Feb/Mar slipping to +55/+58 cents from trade at +62 and +60 cents late on Thursday.
But wet North Sea crudes were looking firmer after several January cargoes found homes with European refiners, traders said.
"There were quite a few deals done privately yesterday at higher numbers," said one.
A third decade Forties cargo was heard sold for around Dated Brent +40/+42 cents a barrel after a mid-month stem was offered for +35 cents. Details could not be immediately confirmed.
Brent loading Jan 15-17, fetched Feb Brent +21 cents on Thursday. Some traders said the price was inflated to influence related swaps trade. Others said it reflected demand strength.
Four Brent cargoes, loading Jan 18-22, were due down the paper chains on Friday. It was unclear whether the holders of the two Jan 17-19 clocked cargoes had been granted deferrals.
In the Mediterranean, Urals talked a touch firmer helped by improved refinery margins but a prompt cargo was still offered by a trader at around Dated Brent -$1.10.
Syria trimmed five cents off its offer for January Light crude but at Dated Brent -30 cents the price was still seen too high for most regular term customers.
Syrian Light was fixed at Dated -5 cents in December.
